data.name: CatThumbnailsDesc
data.value: Preview pictures Explorer built for your photos, videos and documents, plus cached app icons. Explorer rebuilds them as you browse, so folders may show generic icons for a bit.

data.name: CatAvdDesc
data.value: Quick Boot snapshots and the temporary cache of Android emulators from Android Studio. Your installed apps and emulator data are untouched — only snapshots and scratch cache go. Close the emulator first.

data.name: CatDevCachesDesc
data.value: Downloaded packages and build outputs from Maven, Gradle, Cargo and Go. Your tools re-download and rebuild them, so the next build is slower and needs the network. Your projects and settings are untouched.

data.name: CatVirtualDesc
data.value: Sizes only. Virtual disks never shrink on their own, but Purge for Windows never deletes them — a wrong delete destroys the whole machine. Compact or remove each one through its own tool; use the folder button to open it.

data.name: VirtualNote
data.value: Purge for Windows only reports these sizes. Shrink or remove a virtual disk through its own tool — never by deleting its files, or the machine breaks.

data.name: VirtualItemDetail
data.value: Open the folder, then compact or remove it in its own tool.

data.name: WinOldStagingNote
data.value: This includes Windows upgrade staging folders. Only remove them through Windows, and only when no upgrade is in progress.

data.name: WindowsSettingsHint
data.value: Things Windows itself controls. Every change here goes through Windows' own tools, and everything is reversible.

data.name: HibernateHint
data.value: Hibernation saves everything in memory to hiberfil.sys so your PC can fully power off and resume later. Turning it off deletes that file and frees its space, but also turns off Fast Startup, which uses the same file. You can turn it back on any time. Changing this needs admin approval.

data.name: HibernateUnknown
